correctness.rationale: Equality of |P|,|Q| on each full circle yields the rational Schwarz reflection identity for F=P/Q after gcd reduction. Two reflections generate an infinite-order Möbius map except rational transverse angle, and nonconstant rational maps cannot be invariant under infinite-order maps. For angle p pi/q the cross-ratio w maps the circles to lines and rotation fixes exactly C(w^q). Rational-map composition multiplies degrees, forcing q divisibility. Conjugate numerator/denominator zeros prove the real-unimodular U/U-sharp normal form; explicit degree-q pair is coprime. Trigonometric polynomial degree <=d in circle parameter forces equality from any 2d+1 samples. Independently checked constructive pairs for q=2..9 on both image lines numerically; numerical tests not the all-degree proof.

originality.rationale: Chalendar–Partington 2024 already gives irrational/nontransverse two-circle rigidity, rational-angle counterexamples, and a local Taylor-order divisibility restriction. The assessed claim is strictly the global rational-invariant field normal form, q times full reduced map degree, and sharp fixed-degree polynomial threshold. The primary Theorem 2.16 and proof of Theorem 2.1 inspected do not state this complete quotient-degree classification. A differently worded invariant-theory corollary may have appeared elsewhere.
